FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Artificial Limbs, Rehabilitation Appliances and Equipment for the Disabled Sectional Committee had been approved by the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. This first revision of the Indian Standard tvas printed in 1985. In tbe first revision emphasis was given on functional and performance requirements. Only critical dimensions were specified for the whole assembly. The present revision has been taken up to bring it in line with the present manufacturing practices prevailing in the coLLntry. In this revision the dimensions of width and weight have accordingly been modified. The dimension for length (L) and slot have also been modified accordingly. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, tbe final value, obscned or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off \ alLIc shall be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard HIP DISARTICULATION JOINT UNIT FOR LOWER LIMB PROSTHETIC FITMENTS -- SPECIFICATION (Second Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard specifies the dimensional and functional requirement of hip disarticulation joint unit for lower limb prosthetic fitments in artificial limb for amputation at hip level (hemipelvictomy). 2 REFERENCE 3 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS The Indian Standard, IS 4905:1968 `Methods for random sampling', contains provision which, through The shape and dimensions shall be as given in Fig. 1 reference in this text, constitutes provision of this standard. At the time of publication, the edition indicated was valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of the standards.

1S 7373:2003 4 MATERIAL 4.1 The unit shall be manufactured from light weight materials, such as, aluminium alloys and plastic or other suitable material satisfying the test requirements of7.1. 4.2 Materials used shall be such that the total weight of the assembly shall not exceed 340 g for the child size unit and 490 g for the adult size unit. 5 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH located and aligned with respect to the lower limb. 6.1.4 The unit shall have the provision unit into the thigh block. 6.2 Operational 6.2.1 The unit shall have the provision of extension stop which shall arrest the movement of110� with respect to the mid thigh line when mounted on the thigh block. 6.2.2 The unit shall have the provision of extension stop which shall arrest the movement of the joint at 10 to 15� hyper extended position at the hip joint level. The arresting of this movement shall be achieved by using either soft or hard bumpers. The bumpers shall be replaceable to suit individual patient's requirements. 6.2.3 The movement of flexion and extension shall be smooth and free from undesirable frictional elements. Nylon or PVC bush bearings shall be provided to ensure the free movement. 7 TESTS 7.1 Load Test The joint shall be tested for its load carrying capacity by applying the load in the direction which shall simulate the actual conditions when the unit is mounted on the artificial limbs. This is achieved by keeping the unit as shown in Fig. 2 and applying the load at 60� with respect to the side bars. The joint shall not indicate any type of failure when a minimum force of 500 N for child size and 1000 N for adult size is applied. to secure the

All components shall be finished smooth and free from any surface defects. Aluminium components shall be anodized. The cast components shall be free from casting flaws. The side bars shall have a smooth jerk free motion when assembled on the shaft. 6 REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Functional 6.1.1 There shall be provision for ball and socket type of attachment to facilitate appropriate positioning (location) of the unit into the laminated socket when mounted in the artificial limb. 6.1.2 The unit shall have the facility for rotation and medio-lateral shift with respect to the socket to achieve correct alignment after mounting. The ball shall be adjusted through nut and bolt arrangement. 6.1.3 The unit shall have the provision to secure the unit firmly with the socket after it is appropriately

IS 7373:2003 8 MARKING 8.1 The unit shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark and with the size of the unit, that is, child or adult. 8.1.1 BIS Certijcation Marking the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers, maybe obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 9 PACKING The packing shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 10 SAMPLING Sampling scheme and criteria for acceptance shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. However a recommended sampling plan is given in Annex A.

The joint unit may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 8.1.1.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the Iicence for

ANNEX A (Clause 10)
SCALE OF SAMPLING A-1 LOT In any consignment, all the prosthetic fitments produced from the same material and same shape and dimension shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-2 SAMPLING A-2.1 The number of prosthetic fitments to be selected from each lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with COI 1 and 2 of Table 1. A-2.2 These prosthetic fitments shall be selected at random and in order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedures given in IS 4905 shall apply. A-3 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA CONFORMITY All the prosthetic fitments selected FOR
